source_snapshot.procedure: Run OOB `ipmitool ... raw 0x00 0x03 <Control option>` and check post-test logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Commands complete without error and behavior matches each option.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek substitutes `ipmitool chassis power reset`, but that maps to Chassis Control command 02h with control value 03h rather than the source's Chassis Reset command 03h; it also conflicts with the script name `bmc_cold-reset`, which implies App Cold Reset of the management controller.

original_test_intent.purpose: The source appears intended to validate an OOB reset operation, but it does not uniquely identify whether the target is the host/chassis hard-reset function, Chassis Control reset option, or a BMC cold reset; these are distinct operations with different targets and recovery evidence.
original_test_intent.target: Unresolved among: host chassis logic via legacy Chassis Reset (Chassis net function 00h, command 03h, no request data); host hard reset via Chassis Control (command 02h, control 03h); or the responding BMC itself via App Cold Reset (net function 06h, command 02h).
original_test_intent.scope: Cannot be finalized. The item and raw command name legacy host Chassis Reset, the placeholder `<Control option>` and criteria `each option` describe Chassis Control, the merged high-level command uses Chassis Control reset, and the script path names BMC cold reset.
original_test_intent.operation: Do not execute a reset while the owner resolves the three-way conflict. Read-only work may record BMC/host identity, current power/boot/management health and recovery paths, then draft separate command-specific procedures after the intended target is selected.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes. The phrase `each option` suggests multiple operations, while command 03h accepts no option; neither iteration count nor reset type is reliable.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Unresolved. Host hard reset requires loss-and-return of host execution plus boot/SEL/OS evidence; Chassis Control reset has a one-byte 03h request; BMC cold reset may drop the management session and reinitialize controller functions without resetting the host. Command success alone cannot unify these outcomes.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Owner source correction selecting exact command and target; command-specific request bytes; dedicated SUT and maintenance approval; host/BMC/power/console baselines; independent OOB/serial recovery appropriate to the selected reset; exact interruption and recovery timing; boot/SEL/OS or BMC self-test/configuration evidence; workload/data-integrity assessment; no log clearing.
ambiguities: Standard Chassis Reset command 03h has no request data, contradicting `<Control option>` and `each option`.
`ipmitool chassis power reset` uses Chassis Control command 02h with control 03h, not raw command 03h.
The script path says `bmc_cold-reset`, which targets the responding management controller through App Cold Reset rather than host chassis logic.
The source does not define whether host OS, BMC availability, or both should reset, nor their distinct completion criteria.
source_conflicts: Item/raw command, control-option placeholder, high-level command and script path specify three materially different reset tests; choosing one would rewrite the source rather than clarify a parameter.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires a dedicated SUT, explicit approval, one-shot execution, independent recovery, preserved logs and behavioral evidence. It incorrectly accepts `0x00/0x03 <control option>` as a valid command family and treats the problem as a missing option, overlooking that Chassis Reset 03h has no request data and that the source also points to separate Chassis Control and BMC Cold Reset operations.

applicable_history.decision: No locked user decision selects host Chassis Reset, Chassis Control hard reset or BMC Cold Reset. Safety requirements remain applicable but do not resolve test identity.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep execution blocked for a genuine semantic conflict, not merely risk. The source combines three different reset commands and targets; no package or guessed option can determine which behavior constitutes PASS. The testcase owner must split or correct the row before a command-specific automation contract is created.

available_now: Official IPMI definitions distinguish legacy Chassis Reset 03h, Chassis Control 02h/control 03h and App Cold Reset 02h.
Read-only target inventory, current host/BMC health, maintenance eligibility and independent recovery capability can be collected without sending a reset.
V2's generic one-shot reset safety controls remain reusable after the intended operation is selected.
missing_inputs: Owner decision selecting the exact target and command: legacy host Chassis Reset, Chassis Control hard reset, or BMC Cold Reset; split into separate rows if more than one is required
Correct request bytes and removal of the contradictory option/command/script references
Selected-operation-specific expected interruption, maximum downtime, boot/management recovery, preserved-state and acceptance criteria
Dedicated non-production SUT, workload quiescence/data-integrity plan, maintenance approval, independent console/OOB recovery and no-retry escalation
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The testcase and BMC/platform owners must correct the source identity; the lab/workload owner supplies the dedicated window and approval; the recovery owner supplies host or BMC recovery appropriate to the selected operation.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Record exact BMC/SUT/firmware/OS identities, present chassis status, management reachability, console access, workload state and preserved SEL/host logs.
Compare the three normative command definitions and prepare separate draft evidence matrices without transmitting any reset command.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not send raw `0x00 0x03` with an extra byte, substitute `chassis power reset`, invoke BMC cold/warm reset, test `each option`, clear logs, quiesce production workloads or infer intent from the private script name.
Do not auto-retry, batch resets or claim command completion proves host boot or BMC recovery.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The source is corrected or split so each row has one target, one normative command/request, one expected outage/recovery sequence and one evidence set; owners approve the dedicated SUT and recovery; a byte-level dry review confirms no cross-command substitution.

revision_candidate.test_name: Owner Decision Required: Host Chassis Reset versus Chassis Control Reset versus BMC Cold Reset
revision_candidate.purpose: Resolve the source conflict before execution; after correction, validate exactly one selected reset operation and its target-specific recovery behavior on a dedicated SUT.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: No executable environment until the owner selects the target command. Any future execution requires the exact server/BMC firmware, dedicated maintenance window, quiesced workload, independent console and operation-specific recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Mutually exclusive pending choices: host chassis logic using command 03h with no data; host hard reset using Chassis Control command 02h/control 03h; or the responding BMC using App Cold Reset. Do not merge these scopes.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Corrected item/procedure/script mapping; exact command bytes; selected host or BMC target; expected interruption and recovery timing/state; workload/data policy; baseline; maintenance approval; independent recovery; stop/escalation and evidence requirements.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: No reset command is authorized by this candidate. Preserve read-only baseline evidence and return SOURCE_CONFLICT. After the owner corrects or splits the row, create and re-review a separate one-shot procedure for the selected normative command; never translate among the three operations implicitly.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Source conflict resolved in the library; one command/target selected; dedicated SUT and maintenance approval confirmed; workload safely quiesced; logs preserved; independent host/BMC recovery and observers qualified; no automatic retry.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Source-owner decision and corrected revision; normative command mapping; approval and target baseline; then, only after re-review, exact request/completion plus host boot/SEL/OS evidence for a host reset or BMC disconnect/reconnect/self-test/configuration evidence for a BMC reset.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel IPMI 2.0 rev. 1.1 sections 28.3, 28.4 and 20.2 plus the exact platform reset behavior and corrected testcase owner decision.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never guess the reset type, add data to command 03h, substitute a wrapper, reset production/shared systems, clear logs, rely only on command response, auto-retry or use a recovery action not approved for the selected target.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Testcase/BMC/platform owners must first resolve the semantic conflict. A separate fresh lab/workload approval is mandatory immediately before any selected disruptive reset.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Only owners can decide which reset is intended and whether rows must be split. After correction, bounded execution and evidence collection may be automated; workload quiescence, impact judgment and exceptional recovery remain human-controlled.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Undefined until target selection. The corrected row must provide host boot/data recovery for chassis reset or independent BMC recovery for controller reset, with no blind retry and escalation when the selected component does not return within its approved window.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Any unresolved command/target conflict; production/shared workload; missing approval, baseline, observers or recovery; extra request byte for command 03h; wrapper substitution; target mismatch; command/outage beyond bounds; host boot/data issue; BMC non-return; or ambiguous evidence.

identified_defects: The source appends `<Control option>` to a Chassis Reset command that normatively accepts no request data.
The merged high-level command is a different Chassis Control hard-reset operation.
The script path indicates a third operation, BMC Cold Reset, with a different target and evidence.
V2 misses this three-way semantic conflict and therefore proposes an invalid option-byte contract.
Source criteria `each option` and five-minute machine time do not define count or recovery for disruptive resets.
reason_for_change: This is not a missing parameter that can be supplied to one known operation. Normative IPMI command layouts prove that the source combines host Chassis Reset, Chassis Control hard reset and BMC Cold Reset; their targets and completion evidence differ, so V3 must preserve the conflict rather than invent a control option.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7 Markup
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Standard IPMI implementations; exact platform side effects still require vendor evidence
new_technical_evidence.supports: Chassis Reset command 03h has no request data and produces a host hard reset; it is superseded by Chassis Control. Chassis Control command 02h uses a control byte. App Cold Reset command 02h resets the responding controller itself, may not return a response and has platform-specific side effects.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Which of these three operations the testcase owner intended and the target platform's exact recovery behavior remain unresolved.

removed_ambiguities: Explicitly distinguishes three commands that V2 treated as one configurable reset.
States that command 03h has no control option.
Separates host-reset evidence from BMC-reset evidence.
resolved_blockers: None for execution; official evidence establishes the conflict rather than resolving owner intent.
remaining_blockers: The testcase owner must correct or split the source and define target-specific acceptance and recovery before any reset can be reviewed for execution.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents an invalid raw request and possibly resetting the wrong component. It identifies a true semantic blocker supported by the standard instead of treating three distinct operations as one missing option.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Isolated validation confirmed that chassis command 03h, Chassis Control 02h/03h, and BMC App Cold Reset are mutually exclusive operations whose target, execution location, outage, and recovery cannot be inferred. BLOCKED is genuine, discovery remains read-only, no reset is authorized, and completion requires owner correction plus fresh review rather than an agent-selected command or PASS.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The row names Chassis Reset and raw command 03h, requests an undefined control option, links a BMC cold-reset script and merges a Chassis Control wrapper.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 protects disruptive execution but incorrectly assumes command 03h has an option byte and misses the different BMC target in the script.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Permit only read-only baseline and source reconciliation; no reset command can run until the owner selects or splits the three operations.
